# Checked-operation implementation validation

[Issue #82](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/82#issuecomment-6009162442)
records the ordinary decision before production edits. This unit changes the
reserved spelling and diagnostics, retaining `BindOp` / `StaticOpKind::Bind`,
pending common Meaning obligations and the existing finite native evidence gate.

The [integration record](integration-validation-01.json) binds performed
commands, their exact streams and the
[independent review](independent-review-01.json). The
[authoring study](../../../authoring_sessions/checked-operation-v030/README-after-01.md)
retains 16 first projects and 56 actual before/after observations. All 28 AFTER
predictions match: successful controls, phase/tree/runtime/formal/owner
refusals, old-word migration diagnostics and selected unsupported projection.
Source-bearing QIRF identities change naturally; ordered ports and signatures
are compared without imposing whole-artifact equality.

Latest Rust passed 94 focused integration tests plus the one tiny lexer test;
MSRV 1.85 passed 75 plus that lexer test. Both retain two existing ignored
256-receipt/specialization stress tests. Nine new integration tests cover exact
phase/control, stale source bindings, access, locations and lexical migration.
The prepared 10,000-token case was never generated or executed: the
[scope clarification](test-scope-review-02.json) preserves its original code
and the separate finite-versus-selected loading distinction. Its replacement
uses a one-token/two-token internal allowance.

The [CI repair supplement](integration-validation-02.json) records two further
passing tests on each toolchain, bringing the totals to 97 latest and 78 MSRV.
The corpus smoke target checks all 87 current projects and four negative controls;
it is separate from independent mathematical oracle evidence. The preceding
[hosted Rust failure](hosted-predecessor/review-37413163947.json) was a stale
six-snapshot expectation after the two explicit #81 migrations made eight.
Only that test expectation and its explanatory comment changed. Raw #81 logs
also receive narrow Git whitespace attributes, preserving their original bytes.

Both all-target Cargo Clippy runs reject warnings; formatting passed after a
single empty-line repair. Selector tests passed 41 cases. Native retained-
evidence example execution, constitutional continuity against reviewed commit
`faa5cfb5e7ea1cf3b39a43b80f7f2345e89197c2`, VM22/VM29 coverage, edition,
authoring, schema source identity and documentation checks passed. Fixed mdBook
0.5.4 built 26 HTML files; all 1,048 local links and 385 anchors were checked,
including print output. The
[native invocation companion](source-native-environment-02.json) supplies the
explicit inherited CLI selection omitted from the generic runner's summary.

The first strict coverage failures, prepared-source metadata and formatting
failure remain unchanged. VM22/VM29 refresh only the reviewed lexer/lower
identity fields; original inventories are archived. The
[current build binding](current-build-bindings-02.json) retains the original
build lexer and the later `cfg(test)` addition; fixed CLI bytes remain identical.
The [runner](record_validation.py) captures actual command arguments supplied
by the operator. Stored records are evidence, not instructions to execute.

External qargo/qlippy diagnostic work is omitted under explicit maintainer
authorization. No fresh Lean build/audit/replay, universal source preservation,
new guarantee, full-CI/package/installation/native-bundle or release completion
is claimed. Existing scoped guarantees and QS/PR/RS/EXACT pending duties retain
their recorded status. QFT remains outside this development scope.
